{
  "findings": [
    {
      "title": "Primary endpoint analysis method not specified",
      "quote": "The primary endpoint in the study is the percent change in EASI score from baseline to week 16.",
      "page": 27,
      "section": "4.2.1",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "critical",
      "explanation": "The statistical section does not describe the specific analysis method (e.g., mixed model, ANCOVA) for the primary endpoint, only the hypothesis and sample size justification.",
      "fix": "Add a detailed description of the primary analysis method in Section 10.4, including model terms, covariates, and handling of missing data."
    },
    {
      "title": "Secondary efficacy endpoints lack analysis methods",
      "quote": "Proportion of patients achieving EASI-50, EASI-75, and EASI-90 (≥50%, ≥75%, and ≥90% improvement from baseline) at week 16",
      "page": 27,
      "section": "4.2.2",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The statistical section does not specify analysis methods for the secondary efficacy endpoints (e.g., logistic regression, time-to-event analysis for pruritus onset).",
      "fix": "Provide analysis methods for each secondary efficacy endpoint in the SAP or protocol."
    },
    {
      "title": "Missing estimand attributes for primary endpoint",
      "quote": "The primary endpoint in the study is the percent change in EASI score from baseline to week 16.",
      "page": 27,
      "section": "4.2.1",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The estimand for the primary endpoint is incomplete: no explicit definition of the population (beyond 'adult patients with moderate-to-severe AD'), no handling of intercurrent events (e.g., rescue medication, discontinuation), and no summary measure (e.g., difference in means) is stated.",
      "fix": "Define the estimand attributes for the primary endpoint, including intercurrent event strategies and summary measure."
    },
    {
      "title": "Missing handling of missing data",
      "quote": "For continuous variables, descriptive statistics will include the following information: the number of patients reflected in the calculation (n), mean, SD, median, first quartile (Q1), third quartile (Q3), minimum, and maximum.",
      "page": 66,
      "section": "10.4",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The statistical section does not describe how missing data will be handled in the primary or secondary analyses (e.g., multiple imputation, mixed models with missing data assumptions).",
      "fix": "Add a section on missing data handling, including methods for sensitivity analyses."
    },
    {
      "title": "Sample size lacks dropout rate",
      "quote": "the enrollment of 60 patients per treatment group will provide 96% power to detect a 35% difference",
      "page": 66,
      "section": "10.2",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The sample size justification does not account for dropout or missing data, which could reduce power; no dropout rate is mentioned.",
      "fix": "Include an assumed dropout rate and adjust the sample size accordingly, or justify why no adjustment is needed."
    },
    {
      "title": "Inconsistency in sample size wording",
      "quote": "the enrollment of 60 patients per treatment group",
      "page": 66,
      "section": "10.2",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "The phrase 'enrollment of 60 patients per treatment group' is ambiguous: it could mean 60 per group or 60 total. The context suggests per group, but the wording is not explicit.",
      "fix": "Clarify as '60 patients per treatment group' or '60 patients in total'."
    },
    {
      "title": "Exploratory endpoints not analyzed",
      "quote": "Any exploratory endpoints will be described in the statistical analysis plan (SAP).",
      "page": 27,
      "section": "4.2.2",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "The exploratory objectives (e.g., biomarkers, QOL) have no endpoints defined in the protocol, and the SAP is deferred, leaving a gap in the analysis plan.",
      "fix": "List exploratory endpoints in the protocol or ensure the SAP is finalized before database lock."
    },
    {
      "title": "Primary analysis timing may affect multiplicity",
      "quote": "Hence there will be no need for alpha adjustment due to the primary analysis of the study.",
      "page": 68,
      "section": "10.4.3.1",
      "category": "advisory",
      "severity": "advisory",
      "explanation": "The statement that no alpha adjustment is needed for the interim primary analysis is questionable because the same primary endpoint is tested at the interim and final, which could inflate type I error if not properly controlled.",
      "fix": "Clarify the statistical implications of the interim analysis and whether any alpha spending is required."
    }
  ]
}
